Schnittstelle LogAdapter

Alle bekannten Implementierungsklassen:
LogAdapter.DelegatingLogAdapter, LogAdapter.NoOpLogAdapter
public interface LogAdapter

Abstraction layer for logging that allows integration with any logging framework.

This interface decouples the application from specific logging implementations, enabling users to integrate their preferred logging backend (SLF4J, Log4j2, java.util.logging, etc.) through adapter implementations.

All logging methods accept a message and optional arguments. The interpretation of arguments (e.g., parameterized message formatting, exception handling) is delegated to the underlying logging framework implementation.

Implementations should handle the last argument specially if it is a Throwable, treating it as an exception to be logged with its stack trace.

Example usage (syntax depends on the logging framework used): 

    logger.info("Loading plugin", pluginName, version);
    logger.error("Failed to initialize plugin", pluginName, exception);

    • noOpLogAdapter

      static LogAdapter noOpLogAdapter()

      Creates a no-op logger that silently discards all log messages.

      This implementation is useful for testing scenarios or when logging is explicitly not desired. All logging methods perform null checks but are otherwise no-ops.

      Gibt zurück:
      a no-op logger instance; never null

    • delegatingLogAdapter

      static @NonNull LogAdapter delegatingLogAdapter(@NonNull BiConsumer<String,Object[]> debugDelegator, @NonNull BiConsumer<String,Object[]> infoDelegator, @NonNull BiConsumer<String,Object[]> warnDelegator, @NonNull BiConsumer<String,Object[]> errorDelegator)

      Creates a delegating logger that forwards log calls to the provided consumers.

      This factory method enables easy integration with any logging framework through lambda expressions or method references. Each log level is handled by a separate BiConsumer that receives the message and arguments array.

      Example usage with SLF4J: 

          Logger slf4jLogger = LoggerFactory.getLogger(MyClass.class);
    LogAdapter adapter = LogAdapter.delegatingLogAdapter(
        slf4jLogger::debug,
        slf4jLogger::info,
        slf4jLogger::warn,
        slf4jLogger::error
    );
      Parameter:
      debugDelegator - the consumer handling debug-level messages; must not be null
      infoDelegator - the consumer handling info-level messages; must not be null
      warnDelegator - the consumer handling warning-level messages; must not be null
      errorDelegator - the consumer handling error-level messages; must not be null
      Gibt zurück:
      a delegating log adapter instance; never null
      Löst aus:
      NullPointerException - if any delegator is null
      Seit:
      1.0.0

    • debug

      void debug(@NonNull String message, Object... args)

      Delegating logger implementation that forwards log calls to configurable consumers.

      This implementation enables flexible integration with any logging framework by accepting BiConsumers for each log level. Each consumer receives the message and arguments array, allowing framework-specific formatting and handling.

      Instances should be created via delegatingLogAdapter(BiConsumer, BiConsumer, BiConsumer, BiConsumer).

      Seit:

    • debug

      void debug(@NonNull String message)

      Logs a debug-level message.

      Debug messages provide detailed diagnostic information useful during development and troubleshooting. They typically include fine-grained state information and should not be enabled in production environments due to their verbosity.

      Parameter:
      message - the log message; must not be null

    • info

      void info(@NonNull String message, Object... args)

      Logs an info-level message with optional arguments.

      Info messages highlight the progress of the application at a coarse-grained level. They provide general informational messages about normal system operation and significant events or state changes.

      Parameter:
      message - the log message; must not be null
      args - optional arguments; interpretation depends on the logging framework

    • warn

      void warn(@NonNull String message, Object... args)

      Logs a warning-level message with optional arguments.

      Warning messages indicate potentially harmful situations or unexpected behavior that does not prevent the system from functioning. They signal conditions that should be reviewed but do not require immediate action. Examples include deprecated API usage, suboptimal configuration, or recoverable errors.

      Parameter:
      message - the log message; must not be null
      args - optional arguments; interpretation depends on the logging framework

    • error

      void error(@NonNull String message, Object... args)

      Logs an error-level message with optional arguments.

      Error messages indicate serious problems that prevented an operation from completing successfully. They represent failures that require attention but typically allow the system to continue running. If the last argument is a Throwable, it should be logged with its stack trace.

      Parameter:
      message - the log message; must not be null
      args - optional arguments; interpretation depends on the logging framework; the last argument may be a Throwable for exception logging
